purpose: Starter parameter catalog, not a runtime-connected configuration
baselineSource: GDD_Edit_V26 + Edits 37–44, 48 (20–21 October 2026); Edit 49 proposals (49–49.3) tried in P4; Edit 50 in P5; Edit 53 (district-wide traffic) in P5 and the district mock-up; Edit 53.1 (bus routes for P6, a wider Parkland ring); Edit 54 (roundabout lanes by exit, Parkland highway feed, the Chongqing portal, a set piece on every tile); Edit 55 (45° crossing options example, planting and sculpture in three sizes, nothing below ground); Edit 55.1 (crossing rules: A the rule, C centre tile only, D named designs only, B not used); Edit 55.2 (junctions square and central, Parkland ring centred and smaller, walkway joins the highway); Edit 56 (four-way junctions take roundabouts; street and highway ring radii; MUTCD junction markings; a ring orbit cap); Edit 57 (yield-line teeth square to the last straight; Circus layout options); Edit 62 (P6: Waterfront replaces Circus; the game runs Parkland, Waterfront, Monument); Edit 63 (P6.1: managed traffic, edge barriers, rescue sink); Edit 64 (P6.2: one walkway opening per road); Edit 65 (P6.3: stair aprons and screen margins, plans solid, walkway joints)

entries.label: Walk speed
entries.description: Ground speed before run buildup, before terrain modifiers.
entries.purpose: Baseline approach speed; slow enough to read a car's chevron before committing

entries.label: Run speed
entries.description: Full ground run speed before modifiers.
entries.purpose: Twice walk, so crossing a lane costs about one second

entries.label: Walk-to-run buildup
entries.description: Spring start changes the effective value, not this default.
entries.purpose: The cost of starting; removed by Spring start, which is what makes that node felt

entries.label: Turn rate
entries.description: Rotation is proportional: 45° costs one unit, 180° four. The central feel knob
entries.purpose: Rotation is proportional: 45° costs one unit, 180° four. The central feel knob
entries.designBound: Below 90°/s a 180° reversal costs over two seconds and the dummy reads as broken. Above 540°/s turning stops costing time and decision 75 is void.

entries.label: turningSpeedFraction
entries.description: Ground speed while still turning into line; the visible cost of changing direction
entries.purpose: Ground speed while still turning into line; the visible cost of changing direction
entries.designBound: Below 0.4 the dummy stalls while turning and reads as unresponsive. Above 0.85 rotation costs nothing and the scheme collapses to eight-direction.

entries.label: alignThreshold
entries.description: Within this angle of the pressed direction the dummy runs at full speed
entries.purpose: Within this angle of the pressed direction the dummy runs at full speed
entries.designBound: Below 10° full speed almost never engages. Above 60° the dummy runs sideways at full speed and facing stops mattering.

entries.label: Turn startup
entries.description: Time to reach full turn rate.
entries.purpose: Short enough that rotation feels responsive, long enough to read as mechanical

entries.label: Stopping time
entries.description: The coast after the direction input is released. The dummy has mass and does not stop dead.
entries.purpose: The coast after the input is released; the dummy has mass and does not stop dead
entries.designBound: Below 0.1 s the coast is under the threshold of perception and the body reads as weightless. Above 0.6 s the player overshoots into traffic they did not choose, and pillar 1 reads as drift rather than a read.

entries.label: Low-grip stop multiplier
entries.description: How much further the dummy coasts on a low-grip surface. Removed by Grip (Legs, tier 2).
entries.purpose: How much further the dummy coasts on low grip; removed by Grip
entries.designBound: Below 1.5 the diesel spill is not felt and Grip has nothing to sell. Above 4.0 a low-grip surface is a trap rather than a bait, and the player avoids the one place the level wants them to stand.

entries.label: Counter-press angle
entries.description: A press this far or further from the current heading reads as braking rather than steering.
entries.purpose: How far from the heading a press must be to brake rather than steer
entries.designBound: Below 90° every sideways correction brakes and the dummy never flows. At 180° only an exact reversal brakes, so the skill is unusable under pressure.

entries.label: Counter-press stop
entries.description: Fraction of the coast remaining when the player presses back. Applied before the low-grip multiplier.
entries.purpose: How much of the coast remains when the player presses back
entries.designBound: Below 0.2 pressing back is an instant stop and the body's mass disappears on demand. Above 0.8 it is not worth the turn it costs.

entries.label: Lunge distance
entries.description: Fresh-body distance before terrain and wear.
entries.purpose: Reaches a lane from the hard shoulder on a fresh body
entries.designBound: Must reach a lane from the hard shoulder at full health, and must not reach across two lanes, which would remove the need to approach.

entries.label: Lunge duration
entries.description: Duration of nominal lunge motion.
entries.purpose: Too short to abort, which is what makes the commitment matter

entries.label: Lunge recovery
entries.description: Recovery following every lunge.
entries.purpose: Longer than the lunge itself; a missed lunge is punished by exposure

entries.label: Minimum reach fraction
entries.description: Lower bound for damage-shortened lunge reach.
entries.purpose: A fully worn body still reaches a passing car's flank, so pillar 1 holds at any damage
entries.designBound: A fully worn body must still reach a passing car's flank (pillar 1). Above 0.6 wear stops being felt.

entries.label: Capacity
entries.description: Unupgraded capacity; one dash consumes one unit.
entries.purpose: Two dashes before waiting (D19, 20 October)
entries.designBound: Below 2 no bait sequence is possible. At 5 the baseline equals Big battery and that node has nothing to sell.

entries.label: Refill time per unit
entries.description: Seconds to recharge one dash charge with no Battery level. P1–6.8: 0.8. P6.9: 1 ("Dash charge 1s by default"); Battery levels set abilities.battery.level1–3Seconds.
entries.purpose: A full refill takes about as long as a car takes to cross the level

entries.label: Refill delay
entries.description: Delay after a successful charge spend.
entries.purpose: Stops a spent charge refilling mid-lunge

entries.label: Lunge cost
entries.description: D15 remains open.
entries.purpose: One attempt, one charge; the unit the player counts in

entries.label: Additional jump cost
entries.description: Charge one B jump spends, hop or not ("Jump costs 1 battery"). The dash meter pays for both (D15).
entries.source: GDD §§5.4; Edit 75 (27 October): Prototype 6.5; Edit 79 (27 October): Prototype 6.9
entries.purpose: A jump costs a second attempt, so traversal competes with attacking

entries.label: Dash jump cost
entries.description: Charges a jump costs when it leaves a dash (B during a dash). The dash has paid; 0 makes the dash jump always follow a dash. Other jumps cost battery.jumpCost. 6.x builds run 1.
entries.purpose: Dash then jump works on any charge that allowed the dash (user report, 28 October)

entries.label: Tap to put a cone down
entries.description: 1: X with no cone in reach (or the hands full) puts a held cone down at once. Holding X for input.dropHoldSeconds still works. 0: only the hold (6.10).
entries.purpose: A tap picks up, a tap puts down: no hidden hold (user report, 28 October)

entries.label: Baseline cone width
entries.description: Body owns the effective width; Sensing reads it.
entries.purpose: Narrower than human vision; the dummy must turn its whole body to scan
entries.designBound: Below 45° scanning is punitive. At or above 160° — the Wider view value — the upgrade has nothing to sell.

entries.label: Zone fade-in
entries.description: Presentation fade when zones enter the view cone.
entries.purpose: Zones resolve as the cone sweeps, so looking reads as scanning rather than switching

entries.label: Zone opacity
entries.description: Nominal zone drawing opacity.
entries.purpose: Visible without competing with tier-1 cues (4.2)

entries.label: Memory duration
entries.description: Lifetime of proposed last-seen zone snapshots.
entries.purpose: Long enough to turn away and act on what was seen; short enough to stay a memory

entries.label: Ears forecast
entries.description: Target lead time for planned entry, subject to admission delay.
entries.purpose: Warns before a car enters the cone, so the player can turn toward it in time

entries.label: Fresh body health
entries.description: Base (Standard) body health. Edit 40.1 supersedes CR-004 (1600). Difficulty picks proto.health.*.
entries.purpose: Base 800: a body takes several deliberate hits before a write-off
entries.designBound: Below 600 two late sedan lunges (278 each) nearly write a body off. Above 2400 a five-minute visit never reaches a write-off.

entries.label: Base impact
entries.description: Base before zone, lunge, speed and mass factors.
entries.purpose: The reference unit; every other damage figure is a multiple of it

entries.label: Lunge multiplier
entries.description: Also applies to an eligible jump.
entries.purpose: Lunging pays five times standing, which is the anti-standing rule in arithmetic
entries.designBound: Below 3 standing earns more than 45% of a lunge and pillar 1's anti-standing check fails.

entries.label: Head-on share
entries.description: Front impact zone.
entries.purpose: Head-on pays full; the hardest approach pays the most

entries.label: Diagonal-front share
entries.description: Diagonal front impact zone.
entries.purpose: Rewards intercepting a committed route rather than meeting it square

entries.label: Side share
entries.description: Side impact zone.
entries.purpose: A flank hit on a braking car; reachable but cheap

entries.label: Diagonal-rear share
entries.description: Diagonal rear impact zone.
entries.purpose: Near-worthless, to stop players chasing departing cars

entries.label: Rear share
entries.description: Rear impact zone.
entries.purpose: Counts as contact for Non-compliant, pays almost nothing

entries.label: Write-off bonus
entries.description: Score reward only, never chassis damage.
entries.purpose: Larger than any single impact, so finishing a body always beats farming one

entries.label: Combo window
entries.description: A hit within this many seconds of the last hit chains a combo.
entries.purpose: Two dashes, or a bounce into the next car

entries.label: Combo step
entries.description: Each chained hit scores 1 + this × (links − 1) times its points.
entries.purpose: Second hit ×1.5, third ×2

entries.label: Combo cap
entries.description: The combo multiplier's ceiling. P6.5–6.8: 3. P6.9: 5, with scoring.comboVariety.
entries.source: Edit 75 (27 October): Prototype 6.5; Edit 79 (27 October): Prototype 6.9
entries.purpose: ×3 at the fifth hit

entries.label: Wider view width
entries.description: Effective cone width when owned.
entries.purpose: Roughly human binocular plus near peripheral; the first sense returned

entries.label: Hips turn rate
entries.description: Effective turn rate when owned. Under DIRECT (P6.5) Hips has no job and leaves the shop (D48).
entries.status: retired (Edit 77, from P6.7): the shop sells ability tracks by level (proto.abilities). P6.5–6.6 keep it
entries.source: GDD §§5.2, 5.6, 5.8, 9.2; Edit 75 (27 October): Prototype 6.5; Edit 77 (27 October): Prototype 6.7, abilities
entries.purpose: Halves the cost of looking without removing it

entries.label: Spine steering limit
entries.description: Maximum lunge bend.
entries.status: retired (Edit 77, from P6.7): the shop sells ability tracks by level (proto.abilities). P6.5–6.6 keep it
entries.purpose: Enough to correct a misread, not enough to home in

entries.label: Spine steering rate
entries.description: Maximum rate within the bend limit.
entries.status: retired (Edit 77, from P6.7): the shop sells ability tracks by level (proto.abilities). P6.5–6.6 keep it
entries.purpose: The full 45° bend fits inside the lunge duration

entries.label: Neck decoupled-cone speed fraction
entries.description: Movement rate while the view cone is held off the facing; Neck no longer governs sidestep, which is Strafe.
entries.purpose: Moving while looking elsewhere costs speed

entries.label: Jump input window
entries.description: Time from lunge start for second A press.
entries.status: retired (user, 27 October): the jump is its own button (B), not a second A press in a dash
entries.purpose: Early in the lunge only; jumping is a decision, not a correction

entries.label: Jump extension
entries.description: Jump (Legs, B): ground covered in the air, along the input (else the facing). Leg damage shortens it as it shortens the dash.
entries.status: retired (Edit 76, 27 October): distance follows take-off speed (Link's Awakening). Ground covered = take-off speed × upgrades.jumpAirtime
entries.source: GDD §§5.2, 5.6, 5.8, 9.2; Edit 75 (27 October): Prototype 6.5; Edit 76 (27 October): Prototype 6.6 and the jump test
entries.purpose: Clears a car lengthwise and a planter world.jumpableDepth deep

entries.label: Jump airtime
entries.description: Jump airtime in P6.5–6.7 and the jump test's reference. From P6.8 the Legs level sets it: abilities.legs.airtimeBase + abilities.legs.airtimeStep × (level − 1). Ground covered = take-off speed × airtime.
entries.source: GDD §§5.2, 5.6, 5.8, 9.2; Edit 75 (27 October): Prototype 6.5; Edit 76 (27 October): Prototype 6.6 and the jump test; Edit 78 (27 October): Prototype 6.8
entries.purpose: A running jump clears a sedan broadside; a dash jump clears a van broadside

entries.label: Jump height
entries.description: Top of the jump arc (a parabola over upgrades.jumpAirtime), the same at any speed. The dummy clears a car only while above its roof, and a jumpable piece above world.jumpableHeight.
entries.source: Edit 75 (27 October): Prototype 6.5; Edit 76 (27 October): Prototype 6.6 and the jump test
entries.purpose: Over a sedan (19.8) and a van (30.6) at vehicles.scale 0.9; not a bus (43.2)

entries.label: Jump top speed
entries.description: Cap on the jump's take-off speed. A jump during a dash (B in a dash) takes off at the dash's speed, capped here: the long jump.
entries.source: Edit 76 (27 October): Prototype 6.6 and the jump test
entries.purpose: Dash jump covers 162: clears a van broadside, not a bus

entries.label: Jump air steering
entries.description: A normal jump turns its velocity toward the input by at most this per second, at its take-off speed (at least walking pace). No input: momentum holds. A dash jump does not steer.
entries.source: Edit 76 (27 October): Prototype 6.6 and the jump test
entries.purpose: Corrects a jump by about a third of its speed; cannot reverse it

entries.label: Run to clear
entries.description: 1: only a running jump or a dash jump clears anything. A standing or walking jump hops: the body rises, but meets cars, barriers and rails as on the ground. 0: any jump clears what its arc clears (P6.6).
entries.purpose: Speed is the skill: walk and jump, but run to clear

entries.label: Ability tracks
entries.description: 0: the P6.5–6.6 tree. 1: four tracks by level (P6.7–6.8: Battery, Legs, Arms, Throw). 2: three tracks of three levels (P6.9: Battery, Legs, Arms; the throw is Arms 2, the hitch Arms 3). 3: four tracks (P6.10: Battery, Legs, Hands of two levels, Arms the push).
entries.source: Edit 77 (27 October): Prototype 6.7, abilities; Edit 79 (27 October): Prototype 6.9; Edit 80 (27 October): Prototype 6.10
entries.purpose: One track per button; levels shield the ability from damage

entries.label: Ability levels
entries.description: Levels per ability track. Level 1 grants the ability (Battery: a faster charge). P6.9: three tracks (Battery, Legs, Arms), three levels.
entries.source: Edit 77 (27 October): Prototype 6.7, abilities; Edit 78 (27 October): Prototype 6.8; Edit 79 (27 October): Prototype 6.9
entries.purpose: "We only have 3 upgrade levels per asset" (user, 27 October)

entries.label: Wear shield per level
entries.description: Each level of a track cuts its body part's wear on that ability by this share. Battery shields the recharge from torso damage; Legs the run, dash and jump from leg damage; Arms the grip, Throw the throw, from arm damage.
entries.source: Edit 77 (27 October): Prototype 6.7, abilities; Edit 78 (27 October): Prototype 6.8; Edit 79 (27 October): Prototype 6.9
entries.purpose: Level 3 cuts wear by 75%

entries.label: Battery recharge step
entries.description: Each Battery level multiplies battery.secondsPerCharge by this: 0.8 s, then 0.64, 0.51, 0.41 at level 3.
entries.status: retired (Edit 78): the recharge steps linearly, abilities.battery.rechargeCut
entries.source: Edit 77 (27 October): Prototype 6.7, abilities; Edit 78 (27 October): Prototype 6.8
entries.purpose: Faster dash recharge, a dash about every 0.4 s at level 3

entries.label: Ability level 1 price
entries.description: Write-offs (credits) for level 1 of any track. Throw needs Arms level 1.
entries.purpose: Every button's verb for one write-off

entries.label: Ability level 2 price
entries.description: Write-offs for level 2 of any track; needs level 1.
entries.purpose: A run of 9 write-offs buys four level 1s and two level 2s

entries.label: Ability level 3 price
entries.description: Write-offs for level 3 of any track; needs level 2.
entries.purpose: Maxing every track takes 24: several runs

entries.label: Torso recharge loss
entries.description: Torso damage slows the battery's recharge: rate × (1 − this × torso share × (1 − abilities.wearCut × Battery level)).
entries.purpose: Gives torso damage a cost under DIRECT (D46)

entries.label: Torso recharge floor
entries.description: The recharge never falls below this share of its rate.
entries.purpose: A worn torso still recharges

entries.label: Battery recharge step
entries.description: Each Battery level takes this off battery.secondsPerCharge: 0.8 s, then 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.4 at level 4.
entries.status: retired (Edit 79): Battery has a value per level, abilities.battery.level1–3Seconds. P6.8 keeps it
entries.source: Edit 78 (27 October): Prototype 6.8; Edit 79 (27 October): Prototype 6.9
entries.purpose: Linear, like the other tracks; level 4 still empties in a long dash chain

entries.label: Legs 1 airtime
entries.description: Time in the air at Legs 1. The height stays upgrades.jumpHeight.
entries.purpose: A running jump clears a handrail; a dash jump a sedan

entries.label: Legs airtime step
entries.description: Each Legs level after the first adds this to the airtime: 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6 s.
entries.purpose: Legs 2 a dash jump clears a van; Legs 3 a running jump a sedan

entries.label: Cones per Arms level
entries.description: Cones the dummy carries per Arms level: 1, 2, 3, 4. X grabs while there is room; else it places the top cone.
entries.status: retired (Edit 79): Arms carries one cone; its levels are carry, throw, hitch. P6.8 keeps it
entries.source: Edit 78 (27 October): Prototype 6.8; Edit 79 (27 October): Prototype 6.9
entries.purpose: A stack to lay a line of traps

entries.label: Throw range step
entries.description: Each Throw level after the first adds this to upgrades.throwDistance: 120, 160, 200, 240.
entries.status: retired (Edit 79): the throw is Arms 2, at upgrades.throwDistance. P6.8 keeps it
entries.source: Edit 78 (27 October): Prototype 6.8; Edit 79 (27 October): Prototype 6.9
entries.purpose: Linear range, as asked

entries.label: Ability level 4 price
entries.description: Write-offs for level 4 of any track; needs level 3. A track costs 10 in all.
entries.status: retired (Edit 79): three levels. P6.8 keeps it
entries.source: Edit 78 (27 October): Prototype 6.8; Edit 79 (27 October): Prototype 6.9
entries.purpose: Maxing one track takes about a run

entries.label: Newtonian bounce
entries.description: 1: the bounce off a car is the dummy's full post-impact velocity (momentum, proto.restitution, proto.contactFriction; proto.recoilScale 1), then a slide slowed by physics.slideFriction; control returns under walking pace after proto.recoilSeconds. 0: the P2–6.7 recoil (scaled, fading over proto.recoilSeconds).
entries.purpose: Ricochet as physics, not an upgrade

entries.label: Slide friction
entries.description: A knocked dummy slides to a stop at this × physics.gravity × proto.scale.unitsPerMetre (about 120 u/s² at 1).
entries.purpose: A head-on throw slides about 127 units; a flank bounce about 8

entries.label: Gravity
entries.description: Standard gravity, for the slide.
entries.purpose: Physical constant

entries.label: Dummy mass
entries.description: The dummy's mass relative to a sedan (vehicles.sedan.mass 1): about 56 kg to a tonne. Sets the momentum exchange in a hit.
entries.source: Registered Edit 78 from the sim's code (P3 onward)
entries.purpose: A light body bounces off a heavy car

entries.label: Restitution
entries.description: Coefficient of restitution of a dummy–car hit: 0 sticks, 1 bounces back at the closing speed.
entries.source: Registered Edit 78 from the sim's code (P3 onward)
entries.purpose: A dull, plastic hit

entries.label: Contact friction
entries.description: Friction along the contact in a hit: how much a moving car's side drags the dummy along.
entries.source: Registered Edit 78 from the sim's code (P3 onward)
entries.purpose: A flank drags the dummy with the car

entries.label: Recoil scale
entries.description: Share of the physical post-impact velocity the dummy keeps. P2–6.7: 0.6. P6.8 (proto.bounce.newton): 1.
entries.status: user-directed (Edit 83): "the dummy gets hurt which means it doesn't get all the momentum". P7.2: 0.7 with proto.bounce.maxThrow 40; P6.8–7.1: 1
entries.source: Registered Edit 78 from the sim's code (P3 onward); Edit 83 (28 October): Prototype 7.2
entries.purpose: Full momentum from P6.8

entries.label: Recoil time
entries.description: P2–6.7: the recoil fades over this. P6.8: the least time out of control after a hit.
entries.source: Registered Edit 78 from the sim's code (P3 onward)
entries.purpose: A beat before the player steers again

entries.label: Strike speed cap
entries.description: The dummy's own speed counted into a hit is capped here (a dash moves far faster).
entries.source: Registered Edit 78 from the sim's code (P3 onward)
entries.purpose: Keeps a dash's damage and bounce in range

entries.label: Battery 1 charge time
entries.description: Seconds a dash charge takes at Battery 1.
entries.purpose: "battery makes it 0.8, 0.7, 0.6 seconds"

entries.label: Battery 2 charge time
entries.description: Seconds a dash charge takes at Battery 2.
entries.purpose: As asked

entries.label: Battery 3 charge time
entries.description: Seconds a dash charge takes at Battery 3.
entries.purpose: As asked

entries.label: Throw hold
entries.description: Holding X this long with a cone throws it (Arms 2). A shorter press puts it down.
entries.status: retired (Edit 80): a hold of X puts a cone down (input.dropHoldSeconds); the throw retires. P6.9 keeps it
entries.purpose: "Level 2 - long press to throw"

entries.label: Hitch reach
entries.description: Arms 3: X grabs a moving car whose side is within this of the body.
entries.status: retired (Edit 80): Arms is the push off a car (abilities.arms.pushSpeed); the hitch retires. P6.9 keeps it
entries.purpose: Forgiving at speed

entries.label: Hitch time
entries.description: The longest ride before the grip gives.
entries.status: retired (Edit 80): Arms is the push off a car (abilities.arms.pushSpeed); the hitch retires. P6.9 keeps it
entries.purpose: Long enough to pick a target

entries.label: Hitch speed
entries.description: A car slower than this cannot be hitched.
entries.status: retired (Edit 80): Arms is the push off a car (abilities.arms.pushSpeed); the hitch retires. P6.9 keeps it
entries.purpose: Stopped cars are targets, not rides

entries.label: Hitch edge
entries.description: The grip lets go this close to the screen's edge.
entries.status: retired (Edit 80): Arms is the push off a car (abilities.arms.pushSpeed); the hitch retires. P6.9 keeps it
entries.purpose: The sling lands on this screen

entries.label: Sling speed
entries.description: Letting go throws the dummy at the car's velocity × this. The flight is a knock: it slides and strikes as a dash.
entries.status: retired (Edit 80): Arms is the push off a car (abilities.arms.pushSpeed); the sling retires. P6.9 keeps it
entries.purpose: Newtonian: you leave at the car's speed

entries.label: Sling dash
entries.description: A while hitched lets go with a dash: this much speed along the stick, for one charge.
entries.status: retired (Edit 80): Arms is the push off a car (abilities.arms.pushSpeed); the sling retires. P6.9 keeps it
entries.purpose: Aim the sling

entries.label: Combo variety
entries.description: Each new kind of move in a chain adds this to the multiplier: dash, jump, bounce, sling, drop, cone, struck.
entries.purpose: Mix moves to climb faster

entries.label: Combo air time
entries.description: 1: the combo clock stops while the dummy jumps, flies from a hit, rides a hitch or drops. 0: it always runs.
entries.purpose: Air and physics keep a chain alive

entries.label: Cone link
entries.description: 1: a thrown cone that hits a moving car links the combo, once a car.
entries.status: retired (Edit 80): no throw, no cone link. P6.9 keeps it
entries.purpose: Throws join the chain

entries.label: Cone hit points
entries.description: Points for a cone link, × the multiplier.
entries.status: retired (Edit 80): no throw, no cone link. P6.9 keeps it
entries.purpose: Small: a link, not a payday

entries.label: Hands levels
entries.description: Hands has two levels. There is no Hands 3: two hands.
entries.purpose: "There is no Level three (you only have two hands)"

entries.label: Cones per Hands level
entries.description: Each Hands level carries this many more cones: Hands 1 one, Hands 2 two.
entries.purpose: "L1, pick up and drop one, L2, pick up and drop two"

entries.label: Put-down hold
entries.description: Holding X this long with a cone puts it down. A tap picks up.
entries.purpose: "tap once to pick up, press for 0.3s to drop"

entries.label: Push speed
entries.description: Arms 1: Y adds this speed, away from the car just hit or touched (or along the stick).
entries.purpose: A ricochet you time

entries.label: Push step
entries.description: Each Arms level after the first adds this to the push: 160, 200, 240.
entries.purpose: "Stronger arms let your ricochet be stronger"

entries.label: Pushes per Arms level
entries.description: Pushes before landing, per Arms level: 1, 2, 3. They refill on the ground.
entries.purpose: "one extra push each time so you can time it to ricochet more"

entries.label: Push reach
entries.description: Y pushes off a car whose side is within this of the body.
entries.purpose: Touching counts, not only hitting

entries.label: Push window
entries.description: Y within this of a contact pushes off that car, wherever the body has bounced to.
entries.purpose: Time the push after the hit

entries.label: armPushLoss
entries.description: Push speed lost per arm damage share.
entries.purpose: Arm damage weakens the push

entries.label: armPushFloor
entries.description: The push never falls below this share.
entries.purpose: A broken arm still pushes

entries.label: Ricochet bounce
entries.description: Ricochet (Legs, needs Jump): the bounce off a hit goes this many times as fast, so this many times as far.
entries.status: retired (Edit 77, from P6.7): the shop sells ability tracks by level (proto.abilities). P6.5–6.6 keep it
entries.source: Edit 75 (27 October): Prototype 6.5; Edit 77 (27 October): Prototype 6.7, abilities
entries.purpose: Carry the bounce into the next car for a combo

entries.label: Jump landing recovery
entries.description: Jump: after landing, no dash and no jump for this long. The landing keeps the jump's speed; movement does not stop.
entries.source: GDD §§5.2, 5.6, 5.8, 9.2; Edit 75 (27 October): Prototype 6.5; Edit 76 (27 October): Prototype 6.6 and the jump test
entries.purpose: Added to lunge recovery, so jumping is the most exposed action

entries.label: Carry speed fraction
entries.description: Ground-travel modifier while carrying a cone.
entries.purpose: Carrying a cone is a visible, minor handicap

entries.label: Nominal ride limit
entries.description: Safe-detachment exception remains a design/testing issue.
entries.purpose: About one block of travel; a repositioning tool, not a free ride

entries.label: Throw distance
entries.description: Prop travel; wear scaling remains open.
entries.purpose: Places a cone across one lane from the hard shoulder

entries.label: Big battery capacity
entries.description: Effective capacity when Big battery is owned. Base is battery.capacity (2).
entries.status: retired (Edit 77, from P6.7): the shop sells ability tracks by level (proto.abilities). P6.5–6.6 keep it
entries.source: GDD §5.2, 5.6, 9.2; Edit 40 (D26); Edit 77 (27 October): Prototype 6.7, abilities
entries.purpose: One dash more than base: a feint and a strike (D26)

entries.label: Kinetic charge threshold
entries.description: Candidate uses pre-bonus impact damage.
entries.purpose: Only a committed hit refills; glancing contact does not

entries.label: Kinetic refill fraction
entries.description: Fraction of effective capacity.

entries.purpose: Playtest a layout by number

entries.label: Parapet width
entries.description: Deck parapet module, each side. The dummy stands inside it.
entries.purpose: A barrier tile the dummy cannot cross except at a gap

entries.label: Jumpable height
entries.description: Pieces tagged jumpable (terrain column jumpable) count at this height: handrails, parapets, crash and jersey barriers, low planters. A jump clears them above it.
entries.purpose: Handrail height; below a sedan (19.8 at 0.9) plus margin

entries.label: Jumpable depth
entries.description: A Z0 piece is tagged jumpable only if, whole, it is no deeper than this across: one jump crosses it.
entries.purpose: No landing inside a bed

entries.label: Jumpable art height
entries.description: P6 art: a mass drawn no taller than this is a planter, a bed or reeds: tagged jumpable when no deeper than world.jumpableDepth. Edge planters and holds never are.
entries.purpose: Planters and their hedges; not podiums or buildings

entries.label: Deck lamp spacing
entries.description: Street lights stand in pairs, one on each parapet, every this many units: about nine per side across an 800-wide screen. Pale pole, bright head, a light pool on the walkway. Lamps beside a gap are down. P3 and P4 keep 128, staggered.
entries.status: user-directed (22 October): about 8–10 per screen width
entries.purpose: Reads as a highway; the downed lamps mark the drop points

entries.label: Stair length
entries.description: Run of a stair per world.deckHeight of rise, rounded to 16. Z0–Z1 64, Z0–Z2 112, Z1–Z2 48.
entries.purpose: Two tiles: long enough to read as stairs

entries.label: Stair width
entries.description: Width of a stair and of a skybridge.
entries.purpose: One tile; wider than the dummy (26)

entries.label: Stair speed
entries.description: Ground speed multiplier on a stair. No dash on a stair.
entries.purpose: Changing level costs time

entries.label: Drop time
entries.description: Fall from Z1 to the ground. A fall of height h takes × √(h / world.deckHeight): Z2 to the ground 0.47 s. No control, no contact until the landing.
entries.purpose: A short hop: readable, not a dead stop

entries.label: Drop speed
entries.description: Downward speed at the landing after a Z1 fall; × √(h / world.deckHeight) for a fall of height h (Z2 to the ground about 161). Closing speed on a car is its hypotenuse with the car's speed across.
entries.purpose: A landing on a stopped sedan scores 76; on a sedan at cruise, 176. The legs take it
entries.designBound: Above 200 a drop onto a stopped car outscores a full-speed dash.

entries.label: Perimeter wall
entries.description: Thickness of the wall on a district's outer edges (the river closes row 1).
entries.purpose: Half a tile: the district is bounded

entries.label: Boom range
entries.description: A checkpoint boom lifts when a car on its level comes this close.
entries.purpose: About a second at cruise: cars never stop

entries.label: Boom swing
entries.description: Time for a boom to swing fully up or down.
entries.purpose: Up before the car arrives

entries.label: Wall height
entries.description: Drawn height of perimeter walls and checkpoint booths.
entries.purpose: Lower than any building; reads as a boundary

entries.label: Deck crossing angle
entries.description: Within the deck band and one road half-width either side, a road under a flyover runs within this angle of square.
entries.purpose: Flyovers always pass perpendicular to the road beneath

entries.label: Deck column
entries.description: Side of a deck column footprint. Solid on the ground. P5.2: drawn round in section (a lit cylinder on an elliptical base, with a pier cap).
entries.purpose: Wide enough to read as a column below the girder

entries.label: Tight turn radius
entries.description: Centre-line radius of a tight corner, and of each corner of a stepped turn. P4 (Edit 49, proposed): the least bend on any road; no half-radius fallback; inner lane 36.
entries.purpose: A city corner: the inner kerb nearly square

entries.label: Circular turn radius
entries.description: Centre-line radius of a circular turn, where the straights allow it.
entries.purpose: A sweeping bend: cars hold more speed

entries.label: Building setback
entries.description: Forecourt between the pavement and every building front. Spawns stand in it.
entries.purpose: Buildings face the road at one line; the dummy fits beside the pavement

entries.label: Storey height
entries.description: One storey, about 3 m. Buildings are 1 or 2 storeys, or towers of world.towerHeightMin–Max rounded to storeys.
entries.purpose: Single, double and tower read apart by face and shadow

entries.label: Corner acceleration
entries.description: Lateral limit in a bend: speed ≤ √(this × radius), braked for at traffic.comfortBraking.
entries.purpose: Cars slow for tight corners (about 50 at the tight radius): a target
entries.designBound: Above 150 tight corners no longer slow a sedan.

entries.label: Headlight reach
entries.description: Headlight beams follow the route ahead for this distance. They reach the screen before the car.
entries.purpose: About 1.4 s of warning at cruise; objects in a beam cast shadows

entries.label: Headlight strength
entries.description: Beam colour-math strength near the car, in three falloff bands. Day palette × 0.45.
entries.purpose: Visible on dark ground, never brighter than a cue

entries.label: Brake glow length
entries.description: Red wash on the ground behind a braking car.
entries.purpose: A braking car reads from behind, not only by its lamps

entries.label: Brake glow strength
entries.description: Strength of the brake wash nearest the car, in three bands.
entries.purpose: A soft wash: the warning stays the only solid red

entries.label: High level height
entries.description: Height of Z2: the high highway, platform roofs and skybridges, about 18 m. Draws lifted 32 art px.
entries.purpose: Clearly above the low highway; six storeys

entries.label: Skybridge span
entries.description: Longest gap a skybridge crosses between two platform roofs.
entries.purpose: Spans an alley or a service lane, never a road

entries.label: Skybridge chance
entries.description: Chance that the next lot in a row after a platform becomes a platform joined to it by a skybridge.
entries.purpose: Roofs come in joined pairs and threes

entries.label: Platform chain
entries.description: Most platform roofs joined in a row by skybridges.
entries.purpose: A roof walk, not a second street

entries.label: Skybridges per screen
entries.description: Most skybridges on one screen, counting those between rows.
entries.purpose: Keeps the ground readable under Z2

entries.label: Flyover top clearance
entries.description: Least distance from the top screen edge to a flyover as drawn: band top minus its lift (height × proto.art.extrusion). So a Z1 band starts at y ≥ 164, a Z2 band at y ≥ 192. Applies in every district.
entries.purpose: Four 16 px tiles: a dummy entering from above shows before the deck hides it

entries.label: Flyover bottom clearance
entries.description: Least ground between a flyover band and the bottom screen edge: band bottom at y ≤ 512.
entries.purpose: Room for a row of buildings below the deck

entries.label: Shared-edge overlap
entries.description: A building at a shared screen edge reaches at least this far into each screen. Up to 64 into the neighbour where it has room; otherwise the lot keeps world.pedestrianGap off the edge.
entries.purpose: One 16 px tile: the building shows on both screens

entries.label: Follow along the lane
entries.description: A car judges another lane's car only where it stands on this car's own lane ahead (1). 0: a straight strip ahead of the nose, as in P3, which points into the oncoming lane on a bend. The dummy sensor is unchanged.
entries.purpose: No false head-on stops on bends; no mutual stop between opposing cars

entries.label: Jam hold
entries.description: No new car enters a level while one of its cars has been stopped this long and its wait leads, car by car, to a cycle or to nothing. A queue behind the dummy or a cone does not count. 0 turns the hold off.
entries.purpose: A jam never grows (user-directed hold; value proposed)

entries.label: Off-screen jam cleanup
entries.description: A car stopped this long on a screen out of view is removed (P6.1 managed traffic). Cars in view never vanish.
entries.purpose: No jam survives out of sight

entries.label: Roundabout entry radius
entries.description: Centre-line radius of the fillet between a radial road and the ring, at both ends of the route round. Inner lane = this less half a lane.
entries.purpose: Inner lane 68 instead of P3's 4

entries.label: Junction turn radius
entries.description: Centre-line radius of every turn at a priority junction (T, 45° Y, fork). Inner lane = this less half a lane; inner kerb = this less a lane.
entries.purpose: The 96 bus stays within 3 of its lane through a junction turn; at 64 it swings 9 into the next lane

entries.label: Junction approach run
entries.description: A 45° road squared off to meet a road at 90°: the straight run before the junction, on the centre line. Its 45° bend uses world.turnRadiusWide. Lengthens to fit the turn radius.
entries.purpose: Six tiles of square approach, so a 45° road meets the junction as a T

entries.label: Bus swerves
entries.description: 0: a bus only brakes for a hazard and never steers round it (canon: "Only brakes; cannot swerve"). 1: it swerves like the other classes.
entries.purpose: Reads as a bus: a slow wall that stops

entries.label: Bus road radius
entries.description: A bus runs a ground road only if every bend of its centre line on screen keeps this radius (10% polyline tolerance), and never round a ring. Highways (straight) always carry buses.
entries.purpose: The 96 bus stays in its lane: 0 outside at 160, 10 at 64

entries.label: Roundabout arm gap
entries.description: Least ring arc left between two entry fillets where adjacent arms are close (a 45° arm). The fillets shrink to fit, never below world.turnRadiusTight.
entries.purpose: A 45° arm beside a 90° arm without a cusp in the short turn

entries.label: Elevated ring radius (Z1)
entries.description: Centre-line radius of a Z1 elevated roundabout (Parkland). Highway arms join it on fillets of world.roundaboutEntryRadius. One way round, anticlockwise on screen. Edit 53.1: 132 → 200 (user, 25 October: "widen the ring so highways can carry more"). Outer lane 228, inner 172. Edit 55.2: 200 → 160 (user, 25 October: "centred on the screen and slightly smaller"). Outer lane 188, inner 132.
entries.purpose: A ring with a visible hole at the 160 deck width, clear of the top edge

entries.label: Elevated ring radius (Z2)
entries.description: Centre-line radius of a Z2 elevated roundabout. Smaller than Z1: the Z2 lift needs more room under world.deckTopClear.
entries.status: retired (user, 22 October): Parkland keeps one ring, the Z1 ring over the lake
entries.source: Edit 51 (22 October), P5 cityscape mock-up; retired in Edit 51.1
entries.purpose: Fits an 800 × 640 screen with its 32 px lift

entries.label: Walkway ring radius
entries.description: Centre-line radius of the Z1 pedestrian ring round the monument (Monument). Bridges join it to the surrounding malls.
entries.status: retired (user, 22 October): the walkway ring is square, 90° sides and 45° corners (world.walkwayRingHalf)
entries.source: Edit 51 (22 October), P5 cityscape mock-up; retired in Edit 51.1
entries.purpose: The monument stands clear inside it

entries.label: Walkway width
entries.description: Width of a pedestrian walkway or bridge, parapets included. No traffic.
entries.purpose: Narrower than a highway: reads as a footbridge

entries.label: Walkway ring half-size
entries.description: Half the outer width of the square Z1 walkway ring round the monument (Monument). Sides run at 90°; corners are cut at 45°. Its west and east sides bridge both carriageways of the split road.
entries.source: Edit 51.1 (22 October), P5 district mock-up; 168 in Edit 51.2
entries.purpose: The north and south sides stand over the pavements, clear of both lanes

entries.label: Walkway ring corner cut
entries.description: Length cut from each outer corner of the walkway ring, along both sides, at 45°. Each 45° walkway leaves from the middle of a cut.
entries.purpose: A cut wide enough for a 45° walkway to leave it square-on

entries.label: 45° walkway length
entries.description: Open span of each 45° walkway, from the ring's corner cut to the podium roof's face. The walkway runs on inside the roof: flush, no rounded cap. The podiums are placed from it.
entries.source: Edit 51.1 (22 October), P5 district mock-up; redefined in Edit 51.2
entries.purpose: Long enough to read as a bridge; the podium still fits the screen corner

entries.label: Escalators per highway screen
entries.description: Escalators from each highway (Z1 or Z2) down to the ground on every screen it crosses. One on each side, at opposite ends: north at the west end, south at the east end.
entries.purpose: A way up and a way down from either side of the highway on every screen

entries.label: Escalator inset
entries.description: Distance from the screen edge to the near side of each highway escalator.
entries.purpose: Two tiles: clear of the edge, near the end of the highway

entries.label: Split lane offset
entries.description: Where a road splits round an island (the Monument), each lane centre runs this far from the road centre. The lanes leave and rejoin at 45° on fillets of world.roundaboutEntryRadius.
entries.purpose: An island wide enough for the monument and its lamp ring

entries.label: Walkway column
entries.description: Diameter of the round columns under a Z1 walkway. Never in a lane.
entries.purpose: Slimmer than a highway column (world.deckColumn)

entries.label: Ring top clearance
entries.description: An elevated ring's drawn top (lift included) stays at least this far inside the top edge. Rings only; straight highways keep world.deckTopClear.
entries.purpose: Lets the Parkland ring sit in the upper half of its screen without crossing the edge

entries.label: Garden cell width
entries.description: Width of one cell of the park garden grid: a bed and half of the paths either side.
entries.purpose: Five cells across an 800-wide screen

entries.label: Garden cell height
entries.description: Height of one cell of the park garden grid.
entries.purpose: Five cells down a 640-high screen

entries.label: Garden path width
entries.description: Width of the paved path between beds. A light line runs down its centre.
entries.purpose: Room for the dummy to pass between beds

entries.label: Plaza half-size
entries.description: Half the width of the monument plaza's LED-lattice square, corners cut at world.walkwayRingChamfer.
entries.status: retired (user, 22 October): a road now runs through the middle; plazas lie north and south of it
entries.source: Edit 51.1 (22 October), P5 district mock-up; retired in Edit 51.2
entries.purpose: The lattice shows round the walkway ring on all four sides

entries.label: Plaza radius
entries.description: Radius of the monument plaza (Monument).
entries.status: retired (user, 22 October): the plaza is a chamfered square (world.plazaHalf)
entries.source: Edit 51 (22 October), P5 cityscape mock-up; retired in Edit 51.1
entries.purpose: Room for the walkway ring and planters

entries.label: Plaza street width
entries.description: Width of each pedestrian street meeting at the plaza.
entries.status: retired (user, 22 October): no radial streets; only 90° and 45° angles
entries.source: Edit 51 (22 October), P5 cityscape mock-up; retired in Edit 51.1
entries.purpose: One lane wide; paler paving than the plaza

entries.label: Parkland quota
entries.description: Write-offs required in Parkland (district 1 of 3).
entries.purpose: The calm opener

entries.label: Circus quota
entries.description: Write-offs required in Circus (district 2 of 3).
entries.purpose: The busy middle

entries.label: Waterfront quota
entries.description: Write-offs required in Waterfront (district 2 of 3; replaces Circus in P6).
entries.purpose: The busy middle, by the river

entries.label: Monument quota
entries.description: Write-offs required in Monument (district 3 of 3).
entries.purpose: The finale

entries.label: 45° road share
entries.description: Chance that a city screen takes the diagonal style: a through-screen jog as one 45° segment, a corner cut at 45°. Never under a flyover.
entries.purpose: 45° roads occasionally (user-directed); value proposed

entries.label: Jam reverse
entries.description: A car jammed for traffic.gridlockSeconds backs up proto.unstick.reverseGap when the way behind is clear: a car on the wrong side of the road (a pass that met oncoming traffic), a stopped car behind it to make room, or the later of two cars facing each other. 0: P3, no reverse out of a jam.
entries.purpose: Vehicles can reverse out of a pile-up

entries.label: Give-way gap
entries.description: A car stops at its give-way line while a car with priority would reach the shared span within this many seconds, or is in it. Roundabout: circulating cars have priority. Junction (Edit 49.3): the major road, then a left turn off it, then the minor road; the wait also covers the time to clear from a standstill at traffic.acceleration, plus perception.reactionDelay. Cars with priority let in a car that has crossed its line. 0: no give-way (P3).
entries.source: Edit 49.1 (21 October), extended in Edit 49.3; P4 test prototype
entries.purpose: Three- and four-arm roundabouts merge without cars driving through each other

entries.label: Give-way approach speed
entries.description: A car approaching a give-way line slows so that it could stop at the line, reaching it at no more than this speed.
entries.purpose: A car can still stop when a gap closes late

entries.label: Ring orbit lane
entries.description: On (1): a circulating car whose exit is blocked, or that is stuck behind a stopped or crawling car, moves to the inner ring lane and orbits until its exit and the outer lane beside it are clear. Off (0): the inner lane stays empty.
entries.source: Edit 52 (24 October), P5 sim and district mock-up
entries.purpose: Uses the inner lane, as on a real roundabout; a blocked exit no longer stops the whole ring

entries.label: Ring lane change length
entries.description: Distance a car travels while moving between the outer and inner ring lanes (one lane width, world.laneWidth). Its heading swings at most atan(π/2 × world.laneWidth ÷ this): 30° at 150. P4–P5 builds keep 72 (51°).
entries.source: Edit 52 (24 October), P5 sim and district mock-up; Edit 71 (27 October): 72 → 150 in P6
entries.purpose: Cars change ring lanes in a gentle arc, not a swerve

entries.label: Ring exit check
entries.description: Length of exit road checked for a stopped car or the dummy. Something there means the exit is blocked: orbit, or keep orbiting.
entries.source: Edit 52 (24 October), P5 sim and district mock-up
entries.purpose: Two car lengths past the point where the exit leaves the ring

entries.label: Ring merge gap
entries.description: Seconds of closing speed a car needs behind it on the lane it moves into, on top of the two bodies and a margin.
entries.source: Edit 52 (24 October), P5 sim and district mock-up
entries.purpose: A faster car behind is never cut off

entries.label: Ring pass ratio
entries.description: A circulating car may pass on the inner lane when the car ahead on the outer lane goes slower than this share of its cruise speed.
entries.source: Edit 52 (24 October), P5 sim and district mock-up
entries.purpose: Passing only round a stopped or crawling car

entries.label: Ring laps
entries.description: Lap paths built per ring route. Edit 53.1: past the last, the last lap repeats; a car orbits until its exit and the outer lane are clear (no last-lap wait).
entries.source: Edit 52 (24 October), P5 sim and district mock-up
entries.purpose: Long enough for most blocks to clear; never endless

entries.label: Roundabout arms
entries.description: Every roundabout, ground or elevated, has at least this many arms.
entries.source: Edit 52 (24 October), P5 sim and district mock-up
entries.purpose: A ring with two arms is a bend: nobody gives way

entries.label: Highway spacing scale
entries.description: Deck admissions per lane every world.deckInterval times this.
entries.purpose: Fewer cars on the highway: about half as many on screen at 1.4× speed

entries.label: Highway speed scale
entries.description: Deck (highway) cars cruise at their class cruise speed times this.
entries.purpose: Highways run faster: harder hits, less time to read a car

entries.label: Bus share
entries.description: Share of scheduled traffic that is buses. A bus slot on a screen that fails vehicles.bus.minRadius runs as a sedan.
entries.purpose: Buses where the road suits them

entries.label: Police share
entries.description: Share of scheduled traffic that is police (Warden).
entries.purpose: Rare enough to notice

entries.label: Hatchback share
entries.description: Share of a district's scheduled traffic that is hatchbacks. Vans take the district's vanShare first; sedans take what the shares leave.
entries.purpose: The light, quick model of the five

entries.label: District-wide traffic
entries.description: On (1): every screen of a district runs its traffic every tick. A car crossing a shared edge moves to the matching lane next door with its id, model, speed, offset and plan. Cars within world.spawnLeadIn of an edge are seen and drawn next door. The shift's cars enter only where a road or highway crosses the district boundary; at the start every lane runs at its steady headway. Off (0): P5.2, one screen at a time.
entries.source: Edit 53 (25 October), P5 sim and district mock-up
entries.purpose: A car followed across a screen edge is the same car at the same speed (user decision, 25 October)

entries.label: District warm-up
entries.description: The district mock-up runs its linked traffic this long before it is shown, so every screen is already busy.
entries.source: Edit 53 (25 October), P5 sim and district mock-up
entries.purpose: No screen waits for cars (mock-up only)

entries.label: Way out after
entries.description: In the district mock-up a car picks its route afresh at every seam. After this many seams it takes the route with fewest seams to a district exit.
entries.source: Edit 53 (25 October), P5 sim and district mock-up
entries.purpose: No car circles a closed street for ever; the district never fills (mock-up only)

entries.label: Parkland traffic interval
entries.description: Each lane entering Parkland (road or highway) admits one car per 2 × this. The four highway entries all feed the Z1 ring.
entries.source: Edit 53 (25 October), P5 sim and district mock-up; Edit 63 (26 October): 3.2, as Waterfront (equal flow)
entries.purpose: Equal flow with Waterfront under managed traffic (Edit 63)

entries.label: Circus traffic interval
entries.description: Each lane entering Circus admits one car per 2 × this.
entries.source: Edit 53 (25 October), P5 sim and district mock-up
entries.purpose: Busier than Parkland (mock-up)

entries.label: Waterfront traffic interval
entries.description: Each lane entering Waterfront at Z0 admits one car per 2 × this.
entries.purpose: As Circus: busier than Parkland

entries.label: Monument traffic interval
entries.description: Each lane entering Monument admits one car per 2 × this.
entries.source: Edit 53 (25 October), P5 sim and district mock-up
entries.purpose: Steady flow on the one snake road (mock-up)

entries.label: Inner lane by turn
entries.description: A car going this far round a ring (degrees from its join to its exit) takes the inner lane after joining, then moves out in the half lap before its exit. 0: off; the inner lane is for orbiting only.
entries.status: retired (user, 25 October): the inner lane is chosen by exit, traffic.ringInnerExit
entries.purpose: Two circulating lanes where a ring asks for them

entries.label: Z1 ring: inner lane by turn
entries.description: Parkland Z1 ring: cars going to the second exit or beyond (135° or more round) circulate on the inner lane.
entries.status: retired (user, 25 October): the inner lane is chosen by exit, traffic.ringInnerExit
entries.purpose: The widened ring uses both lanes (user, 25 October)

entries.label: Ring fill limit
entries.description: A car joins a ring only while the cars on it (length plus traffic.minimumGap each) fill less than this share of the outer lane. 0: off.
entries.purpose: A full ring locks; a metered ring keeps moving and queues wait on the arms

entries.label: Z1 ring: fill limit
entries.description: Parkland Z1 ring: entry metering at half the outer lane.
entries.purpose: Four highways at the game rate without a lock

entries.label: Bus routes per district
entries.description: The P6 planner builds at least this many whole bus routes per district, edge to edge, every bend at vehicles.bus.minRadius or wider, no ring. Buses enter only on bus routes.
entries.purpose: Ground buses back in the game (user, 25 October)

entries.label: Inner lane from this exit
entries.description: Only a car leaving a ring at this exit or later (counted round from its own arm) moves to the inner lane after joining; it moves out in the half lap before its exit. 3 on four arms: the third exit, 270°. A car whose exit is blocked goes round again and may use the inner lane. 0: off; the inner lane is for orbiting only.
entries.purpose: Cars turning 90° or 180° keep the outer lane (user, 25 October)

entries.label: Ring: most orbiting cars
entries.description: A car whose ring exit is blocked waits at the yield line once this many cars already orbit that ring. Orbiters no longer fill a ring and lock the roads round it. 0: off; every car enters and orbits.
entries.purpose: Circus locked at 13 minutes once every four-way became a ring; 2 holds 35 minutes at design flow

entries.label: Parkland: highway entry interval
entries.description: Parkland mock-up: seconds between cars entering at each highway end on the district edge. Its four highways all feed the Z1 ring.
entries.purpose: Free-flowing highways at the game density (about 0.5 cars per lane per screen)

entries.label: Waterfront: bridge entry interval
entries.description: Waterfront: seconds between cars entering each bridge lane at the south edge. The bridges end at T junctions on the ridge road and give way there.
entries.purpose: Free-flowing highways at the game density (about 0.5 cars per lane per screen)

entries.label: Portal headroom
entries.description: Where a highway runs through a tower, the opening rises this far above the deck. The tower rises at least two storeys (world.storeyHeight) above the opening.
entries.purpose: A highway through a building, Chongqing style (user, 25 October)

entries.label: Junction stagger
entries.description: Option B for a 45° crossroads (example only): the 45° road meets the major road at two T junctions this far apart, each squared to 90°. Crossing traffic turns left onto the major road, then right off it.
entries.status: retired (user, 25 October): staggered T junctions are not used; only options A and C were accepted
entries.purpose: Two fillets of world.junctionTurnRadius and a queue fit between the junctions

entries.label: Garden: large unit
entries.description: A great lawn covers the largest free block of garden cells, at least this many cells square and at most one cell more each way; paths inside it go. One per tile where room allows.
entries.purpose: The large unit of the planting hierarchy (user, 25 October)

entries.label: Garden: bed types
entries.description: Most medium bed types on one tile. Beds framing the great lawn take the first; beds framing the set piece the second.
entries.purpose: Medium beds read as one family

entries.label: Garden: small planter
entries.description: Width of a small planter (a concrete box with a clipped hedge top). Two to each open square, one at each corner of the great lawn.
entries.purpose: The small unit: about a third of a bed across

entries.label: Sculpture: large
entries.description: Scale of a sculpture court's centrepiece against a medium piece.
entries.purpose: The large piece of the sculpture hierarchy

entries.label: Sculpture: small
entries.description: Scale of the small pieces: lit bollards, 8 art px tall at 0.5.
entries.purpose: The small piece of the sculpture hierarchy

entries.label: Sculpture court: small pieces
entries.description: Lit bollards in a row along a sculpture court's front edge.
entries.purpose: A rhythm under the centrepiece and its pair

entries.label: Junction zone
entries.description: Every junction sits inside this central share of its tile, each way (0.75: x 100–700, y 80–560 on an 800 × 640 screen).
entries.purpose: No junction cut by a screen edge (user, 25 October)

entries.label: Street roundabout radius
entries.description: Centre radius of a ground (street) roundabout in the district plans. Outer lane 140, inner 84, central island to the inner kerb. Highway rings keep world.deckRingRadius; the P5 game keeps world.roundaboutRadius until P6.
entries.purpose: Smaller rings for streets, larger for highways (user, 26 October)

entries.label: Yield line: tooth base
entries.description: Yield-line tooth base along the line. 7 art px: an odd width gives a one-pixel apex. Teeth are stamped identical, at equal steps, pointing back up the approach lane's last straight (Edit 57).
entries.purpose: US junction markings (user, 26 October)

entries.label: Yield line: tooth height
entries.description: Yield-line tooth height: 1.5 × base (MUTCD 3B.16). On a 45° approach the tooth edges run 1 : 2 and 2 : 1, clean in pixels (Edit 57).
entries.purpose: US junction markings (user, 26 October)

entries.label: Yield line: gap
entries.description: Gap between yield-line teeth. Three teeth span 50 of the 56 lane (Edit 57).
entries.purpose: US junction markings (user, 26 October)

entries.label: River rescue: sink
entries.description: Seconds the dummy sinks in the river before the rescue drone flies in from the screen edge (D37).
entries.purpose: The fall reads; the rescue takes time

entries.label: Stair apron
entries.description: Clear ground beyond a ground stair's foot, across its width plus 8 each side. Nothing stands in it: no building, pool, planter or other flight. At least 2 × body.radius + 12.
entries.purpose: The dummy always fits into a flight

entries.label: Stair edge margin
entries.description: A flight as drawn (its head lifted by its level) and its apron stay this far inside the screen.
entries.purpose: No flight runs off the screen

entries.label: Edge arrival room
entries.description: The dummy may cross a screen edge only where, on the far side, it can be pushed out to standing room within body.radius along the edge or this far in. Else the near side shows a planter. An edge that holds holds all along, behind buildings and lawns too.
